title: Algebraicity Transfer and Integral Hodge Defects: Construction, Return, and Matroidal Obstructions
content: Let X be a smooth complex projective variety and let L⊆H2p(X,Z(p))Hdg/tors be a finite-rank integral Hodge sector. We compare the constructional lattice Acon, the intrinsic cycle-class lattice Aact, and an independently established obstruction lattice Aobs, with Acon⊆Aact⊆Aobs⊆L. For a Chow-compatible transfer--return system satisfying r∘u=midL, algebraicity of the transported sector implies mL⊆Aact and exp⁡Dact∣m. We apply this framework to finite trace, support enlargement, Jacobian targets, minimal classes on principally polarized abelian varieties, and matroidal degenerations. If a smooth projective connected curve maps to a principally polarized abelian variety A with cohomology class qαA, its induced Jacobian transfer and polarized return have multiplicity q2. Combining this quadratic return law with known divisibility and optimality results yields (exp⁡Dact,ρJcurv,μJcurv)=(2,4,4),(2,4,4),(6,36,36) for very general ppavs of dimensions 4, 5, and 6. These examples separate intrinsic integral defects from the multiplicities of a specified geometric return mechanism.
